name: Square
tagline: Payment processing, point of sale, and a merchant account for small businesses, bundled into one signup.

pricing.basis: percentage plus fixed fee per transaction
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software part of Square is genuinely unremarkable: a product catalog, a cart, a receipt, a sales report. An agent can clone that in an afternoon and it will feel fine. What you cannot one-shot is being allowed to touch other people's card numbers: that requires card network membership or a sponsor bank, KYC and AML programs, PCI DSS scope, underwriting, chargeback handling, and the capital to float settlement before the money clears. Square's actual product is the fact that a stranger can sign up on Tuesday and have money in their bank Thursday without ever talking to a bank. Build the register if you want; you will still be renting the payment rails from someone, and that someone charges roughly what Square charges.
coreLoopDIY: A local point of sale with catalog, cart, tax, receipts, and a sales ledger, charging cards through a third-party processor's API rather than your own rails.
requirements: Node 20+ and a machine that stays on during business hours
An account with a licensed payment processor for any real card charges
A public HTTPS endpoint for payment webhooks
A tablet or laptop for the register, plus a receipt printer if you want paper
whatYouLose: Actual card acceptance: you are still a tenant of some processor's merchant account, not the middleman
Fast predictable payouts and the balance-sheet risk Square eats on your behalf
PCI scope offloading, fraud screening, dispute and chargeback handling
Certified card-present hardware: readers, taps, EMV, encrypted key injection
The attached ecosystem people quietly rely on: invoices, payroll, capital loans, buy-now-pay-later, gift cards
Offline mode and polished native apps that keep working when wifi dies mid-queue
moatNotes: Payments is a regulated balance-sheet business wearing a software costume. The app is the thin part.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the alternative to Square is a conversation with a bank's merchant services department, a three-week underwriting process, a monthly minimum, a statement you cannot read, and a terminal lease. Square replaced all of that with a signup form and a flat rate, and it carries the fraud loss, the dispute paperwork, and the regulatory burden that comes with it. The per-transaction fee is not a software subscription, it is the price of someone else holding the licenses and the risk. Most merchants would pay more to escape it, not less.
notes: The register is a weekend; the rails are not. The moat is card network membership, sponsor banking, and the underwriting appetite to onboard strangers in five minutes.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted point of sale and sales ledger for one small business, run on a local machine.

Be honest about scope up front in the README: this does NOT process cards on its own. Card acceptance requires a licensed acquirer or payment facilitator, so this app integrates one and keeps the ledger.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Stripe Node SDK in test mode. No auth provider, no hosted database, no telemetry. Single operator assumed, protected by one shared PIN stored hashed in .env.

In scope:
- Catalog: items with name, SKU, price in cents, tax category, optional variants, optional image path on disk.
- Register screen: tile grid, tap to add to cart, quantity steppers, line discounts, order-level discount, tax calculated per category from a configurable rate table.
- Tender: cash (with change due), external card (operator records that a terminal approved it), and Stripe Checkout in test mode for a card-not-present link shown as a QR code.
- Stripe webhook route that marks orders paid, with signature verification and idempotent handling.
- Receipts: printable HTML receipt at /receipt/[orderId], plus optional email receipt via SMTP creds in .env.
- Ledger: immutable orders table, append-only refund records, daily close report with gross, tax, discounts, refunds, and tender breakdown.
- Inventory: simple stock counts decremented on sale, low-stock list.
- CSV export of orders and line items for accounting.

Out of scope, state this explicitly and do not stub it: EMV or NFC card-present processing, PCI-scoped card entry, payouts or settlement, chargeback workflows, multi-location, payroll, loans.

Store money as integers only. Never store card data in SQLite, not even last four from manual entry. Keep all secrets in .env with a committed .env.example.

Deliver: schema file, seed script with ten sample items, one command to run (npm run dev), and a README that says plainly which parts of Square this replaces and which parts you are still renting.
